question.text: Per NISM Series VIII, what is the formula for the number of index futures contracts an investor must SHORT to fully hedge the systematic risk of an equity portfolio?

answer.text: Portfolio Beta multiplied by Portfolio Value, divided by (Index Futures Price multiplied by Lot Size)
Portfolio Value divided by (Index Futures Price multiplied by Lot Size), with no beta adjustment
Portfolio Beta multiplied by Index Futures Price, divided by Portfolio Value
Portfolio Beta multiplied by Lot Size, divided by Portfolio Value

explanation.text: The Logic: NISM Series VIII (Equity Derivatives) gives the index-futures hedge ratio for an equity portfolio as: number of contracts to short equals Portfolio Beta multiplied by Portfolio Value, divided by (Index Futures Price multiplied by Lot Size). Selling this number of index futures offsets the portfolio's systematic (market) risk, leaving only the residual stock-specific risk. The Trap: Option B drops the beta adjustment and would over- or under-hedge whenever the portfolio's beta is not 1.0. Options C and D rearrange the variables so the units no longer give "number of contracts". Note: The item was rewritten around the workbook-backed full-hedge formula (which Series VIII states directly) instead of the prior change-of-beta formula that was not stated verbatim in the checked source. The explanation now spells out the relationship in words to avoid the malformed-symbol issue, and the unsupported Cross-Exam Context and Pro-Tip paragraphs were removed.
